headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk via shared MCP surfaces; OpenBBTerminal’s broader I/O makes cascading misuse plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP server and OpenBBTerminal also uses MCP servers, so a shared bridge is plausible. MemMachine treats conversational context and long-term user facts as inputs, while OpenBBTerminal can consume external data through its APIs. That creates an interaction path where attacker-controlled content from one agent can be interpreted by the other as instructions or trusted context.
conditions: IF both agents are connected through the same MCP server or message bridge
IF OpenBBTerminal forwards untrusted content from MemMachine into tool prompts without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared MCP routing between the agents
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages
Require a human review step before executing tool-derived instructions
Restrict MemMachine outputs to structured, non-instructional fields
requires-engineering: implement allowlisted prompt schemas between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, and OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. Both expose API/MCP surfaces, so if they share a workspace or transport, sensitive data can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs. The profiles do not show direct filesystem sharing, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF the agents exchange prompts or files through a shared MCP server
IF either agent logs or echoes the other’s context into user-visible output
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Turn off verbose logging for cross-agent traffic
Redact financial and long-term user facts before handoff
Use per-agent API credentials
requires-engineering: add field-level data-loss prevention on shared channels

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine has allowlisted network egress and MCP access, while OpenBBTerminal has no network egress, no filesystem write, and no git modification. The overlap is mainly read/transport through MCP, so direct write-write conflict is limited. Because the shared mutable surface is not documented, uncertainty stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable MCP-backed resource
IF an orchestrator grants OpenBBTerminal write access not shown in its profile
mitigations: Keep OpenBBTerminal read-only
Avoid shared mutable MCP resources
Assign separate credentials per agent
Monitor for concurrent updates to shared endpoints

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can surface long-term user facts and preferences, and OpenBBTerminal can act on financial data through APIs. If OpenBBTerminal treats MemMachine output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated fact can cascade into incorrect financial analysis or downstream actions. The profiles do not show explicit verification gates, so the safer assumption is a default-path risk.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes MemMachine output without validation
IF MemMachine emits stale or user-influenced facts that OpenBBTerminal reuses as ground truth
mitigations: Insert a verification step before OpenBBTerminal acts on MemMachine output
Label MemMachine content as advisory only
Require source citations for any transferred facts
Limit automated actions to read-only analysis
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data. That combination can create retention and subject-rights mismatches if the pair shares logs or exports. Only one agent needs citation for the compliance mismatch itself, but both are cited because the risk arises from their combined data classes and surfaces.
conditions: IF shared logs retain both conversational memory and financial records beyond policy
IF deletion or export requests are handled inconsistently across the two agents
mitigations: Align retention settings across both agents
Document deletion/export handling for shared records
Minimize stored personal and financial fields
Review whether any shared logs contain regulated data
requires-engineering: implement unified retention and DSAR workflows
